name: Mission Bay
thesis: Institutional gravity. UCSF, Mission Rock, and the AI campus along Third are rewriting the east-of-101 waterfront as a single decision, not a collection of buildings.
signal: Compression on the waterfront, overflow into the 8.1 msf SF office demand stack. 36% of that stack is AI-related.

name: South San Francisco
thesis: The purpose-built life-science core. Oyster Point and the Forbes/East Grand shelf still clear the largest lab requirements — and they are where new-construction comps actually printed.
signal: Product, not vacancy, is the constraint. Lab-ready and campus-adjacent space is what moves.

name: Peninsula
thesis: Office and life science share a corridor but not a product. Demand is real; the mismatch is lab, power, and adjacency — not a missing building count.
signal: Peninsula office printed 23.8% vacant and −93k SF in Q4, with ±2.7 msf of demand still in the market. Product — not a missing building — is the constraint.

name: Silicon Valley
thesis: 139.3 million SF of R&D is not one bid. Palo Alto still prices like a scarce product. Fremont/Newark absorbed when the rest of the Valley gave space back.
signal: Large-block seekers (100k+ SF) are 41.6% of the demand stack. Average vacancy hides that split.
